# kapitan — full reference for LLMs

kapitan is a type-first, commander.js-like CLI framework for Node.js. This file
is the complete, self-contained reference: read it end-to-end before generating
kapitan code. Everything here reflects the actual public API in `src/index.ts`.

Golden rules when writing kapitan code:
- The ONLY public entry points are the `program` singleton and the `Program` /
  `Group` / `Command` / `CliError` types. Never import from `src/*` internals.
- Never annotate the `action` callback's parameter — the builder infers it.
- Never annotate function return types (repo convention).
- Option/argument names are declared in kebab-case and READ in camelCase.
- The builder is order-free within a node; `.start()` / `.startAsync()` come last.

## Import surface

```ts
import { program } from 'kapitan';
import type { Program, Group, Command, CliError } from 'kapitan';
```

`program` is a shared singleton (one per process). A CLI is defined by chaining
builders on it and finishing with `program.start()` (sync) or
`program.startAsync()` (async). There is no `new Program()`.

## Node kinds

- program (root): the singleton. Has options, arguments, inject, hooks, children,
  action, `.version()`, `.description()`, `.config()`, `.start()`, `.startAsync()`.
- group: opened with `.sub(name)`. Holds child commands/groups, options, inject,
  hooks, `.description()`. Has NO `.action()` and NO `.argument()`.
- command (leaf): opened with `.command(name)`. Has options, arguments, inject,
  hooks, `.action()`, `.description()`. Has NO children.

Parent options, injected values and hooks are inherited by every descendant.

## Builder methods (exact signatures & semantics)

### .version(v: string)  — root only
Enables the built-in `--version` / `-V`. One-shot. Order-free with
`.description()`: both `.version(x).description(y)` and `.description(y).version(x)`
compile. Once any body method (option/command/…) is called, both drop.

### .description(text: string)  — program / group / command
Sets the header line shown in `--help`. One-shot per node.

### .config(config: ProgramConfig)  — root only
```ts
type ProgramConfig = {
  dateFormat?: string;      // fecha token format for 'date'     (default 'YYYY-MM-DD')
  dateTimeFormat?: string;  // fecha token format for 'datetime' (default 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss')
  errorHandler?: (errors: CliError[]) => void; // see "Errors"
};
```
Format literals are validated at COMPILE TIME against fecha's token subset (see
"Option types"): a miscased/unknown token is a type error. `dateFormat` accepts
date tokens only; `dateTimeFormat` also accepts the time tokens.

### .option(name, opts?)  — program / group / command
Declares a flag and GROWS the resolved options type. `name` is kebab-case; the
resolved key is camelCase.
```ts
type OptionOptions = {
  required?: boolean;   // required → key is non-optional in the options type
  default?: unknown;    // presence of a default also makes the key non-optional
  type?: OptionsOptionType;         // see "Option types"
  array?: boolean;      // true → repeatable; value is T[]
  description?: string; // shown in --help
  var?: string;         // store under this key instead of the flag name
  alias?: (string | { name: string; short?: boolean })[];
  //   'out'                    → long alias  --out
  //   { name: 'o', short: true } → short alias -o
  //   { name: 'out' }          → long alias  --out
};
```
Overloads: `.option('name')` (bare string flag), `.option('name', opts)`, and a
`var` overload storing under `opts.var`. Redeclaring an existing key or flag is a
compile-time error (the name/flag type resolves to `never`).

### .inject(name, valueOrFactory)  — program / group / command
Adds an always-present, non-CLI value to `options`. Pass a value or a
zero-arg factory `() => T`; the resolved type is `T` (or the factory's return).
```ts
program.inject('now', () => new Date());   // options.now: Date
program.inject('config', loadedConfig);    // options.config: typeof loadedConfig
```

### .argument(name, opts?)  — program / command
Declares a positional. Same type/coercion rules as options.
```ts
type ArgumentOptions = {
  required?: boolean;   // required or has default → non-optional key
  default?: unknown;
  type?: OptionsOptionType;
  array?: boolean;      // collects trailing positionals into an array
  description?: string;
};
```
Read via `args` (camelCased). Bare `.argument('name')` resolves to
`string | undefined`.

### .hook(fn)  — program / group / command
`fn(options)` runs BEFORE the action, with the fully-resolved options for the
node. Group hooks run ancestor→leaf, then the leaf's own hook, then the action.
Sync hook: `(options) => void`. Async hook: `(options) => Promise<void>` —
awaited only by `startAsync()`; `start()` throws if a hook returns a promise.

### .sub(name)  — program / group  → Group
Opens a nested group (namespace). Chain `.option()/.hook()/.command()/.sub()` on
it. No action.

### .command(name)  — program / group  → Command
Attaches a leaf command. Chain options/arguments/hook/description, finish with
`.action()`.

### .action(fn)  — program / command
Terminal handler. Receives ONE object:
```ts
.action(({ command, options, args, rest }) => { /* … */ })
```
- `options`: `{ [flag]: T }` typed from every `.option()` / `.inject()` in scope.
- `args`: `{ [name]: T }` typed from every `.argument()`.
- `rest`: `string[]` — raw tokens after the first bare `--` (always present, `[]`
  when none).
- `command`: `string | undefined` — resolved command path.
Return value may be a promise (then use `startAsync()`).

### .start()  — root only
Parses `process.argv`, dispatches to the resolved command. Throws if the action
or any hook is async (use `startAsync()` instead). If parsing produced errors,
the action does NOT run — the error handler is invoked instead.

### .startAsync()  — root only
Async variant: awaits hooks and the action. Returns `Promise<void>`.

## Option types (`type` field)

`OptionsOptionType` is one of:
- `'string'` (default) → `string`
- `'boolean'` → `boolean`. Bare `--flag` = `true`; `--flag=false` = `false`;
  `--flag=true` = `true`.
- `'number'` → `number` via `Number.parseFloat`; non-numeric → `invalid-value`.
- `'date'` → `Date`, parsed by fecha with `dateFormat`; invalid/out-of-range →
  `invalid-value` (carries `format`).
- `'datetime'` → `Date`, parsed by fecha with `dateTimeFormat`.
  Supported tokens (a non-localized subset of fecha's moment.js tokens):
    date:      YYYY YY MM M DD D
    datetime:  + HH H hh h  mm m  ss s  SSS SS S  A a  ZZ Z
  Separators: `-` `/` `:` `.` and space. NOT supported: localized name tokens
  (MMM/MMMM months, ddd/dddd days) — kapitan is numeric-only + AM/PM. fecha is
  strict: fixed-width tokens reject `2026-7-3`; overflow (`2025-02-30`, hour 24)
  → null → `invalid-value`. Note the casing is moment-style (UPPERCASE `DD`/`MM`/
  `YYYY`), NOT date-fns (`dd`/`yyyy`) — the compile-time check flags that habit.
  ESCAPE HATCH: set `dateFormat`/`dateTimeFormat` to the sentinel `'js'` to bypass
  fecha and delegate to the platform `new Date()` parser (ISO 8601 + engine
  extras) — for machine timestamps like `.toISOString()`. Laxer than fecha and
  timezone-footgunned (date-only → UTC, date-time-without-offset → local);
  validity is still enforced (unparseable → `invalid-value`).
- `readonly [...]` enum tuple, e.g. `['dev','staging','prod']` → the union
  `'dev' | 'staging' | 'prod'`; anything else → `invalid-enum` (lists choices).
- `(value: string) => T` custom parser → `T`; throw inside it to reject (becomes
  `invalid-value` with your message).

`array: true` wraps the resolved type in `T[]` and collects one entry per
occurrence of the flag (comma is NOT a separator).

## Parsing behavior (important details)

- kebab→camel: `--dry-run` is read as `options.dryRun`; `deploy-target` →
  `deployTarget`.
- `=` vs spaced: `--port=8080` ≡ `--port 8080`. A spaced value may begin with `-`
  only if it looks like a negative number; otherwise → `missing-value`.
- Short-flag clustering: `-abc` = `-a -b -c`. Arity-0 flags emit and continue;
  the first value-taking flag consumes the remainder (`-p8080`, one `=` stripped).
  Unknown cluster char → `unknown-option`. `-5` stays a positional.
- Repeated options: array option collects each occurrence; non-array repeated →
  `duplicate-option`.
- `--` passthrough: the first bare `--` ends option/command parsing; everything
  after it is collected raw into `rest`. Named positionals only draw from tokens
  BEFORE the `--`.
- Built-ins: `--help`/`-h` always recognized (never error, no config to disable).
  `--version`/`-V` recognized only after `.version()`. Declaring your own
  `--help`/`--version`/`-h`/`-V` overrides the built-in. `--no-help`/`--no-version`
  are NOT special (→ `unknown-option`). A group invoked with no sub-command prints
  its help (a `missing-command` situation rendered as help).

## Errors

Parsing accumulates all errors in one pass, then reports the batch ONCE; the
action never runs if any error occurred. Default handler: write each `.message`
to `stderr`, then `process.exit(1)`.

Custom handler OWNS termination (no exit is forced — the dispatcher already
aborts by not running the action):
```ts
program.config({
  errorHandler: (errors) => {                 // errors: CliError[]
    for (const e of errors) console.error(`[${e.code}] ${e.message}`);
    process.exit(2);
  },
});
```

`CliError` shape:
```ts
type CliError = {
  code: CliErrorCode;
  message: string;   // ready-to-print
  token: string;     // identifier AS INVOKED: '-c', '--name', a positional name,
                     // or a command chain ('remote add', '' at root)
  value?: unknown;   // offending input: string, or string[] for too-many-arguments
  type?: OptionOptions['type']; // what was expected
  format?: string;   // date/datetime format that was expected
};
type CliErrorCode =
  | 'unknown-option' | 'duplicate-option' | 'missing-value' | 'missing-required'
  | 'invalid-value'  | 'invalid-enum'     | 'unknown-command' | 'missing-command'
  | 'missing-argument' | 'too-many-arguments';
```
Notes: `too-many-arguments` is ONE error for the whole surplus (`value` is the
`string[]` of extra tokens, `token` is the command chain). `missing-required` →
`Missing required parameter '--name'`. `invalid-enum` →
`Invalid value 'x' for '--env' (choices: dev|staging|prod)`.

## Complete examples

### 1. Single command, mixed types
```ts
import { program } from 'kapitan';

program
  .version('1.0.0')
  .description('Start the server.')
  .option('name', { required: true })
  .option('env', { type: ['dev', 'staging', 'prod'], default: 'dev' })
  .option('port', { type: 'number', default: 3000 })
  .option('verbose', { type: 'boolean', alias: [{ name: 'v', short: true }] })
  .action(({ options }) => {
    // options: { name: string; env: 'dev'|'staging'|'prod'; port: number; verbose?: boolean }
    console.log(options);
  });

program.start();
```

### 2. Nested commands with inherited parent option
```ts
program
  .option('verbose', { type: 'boolean' }) // inherited by deploy
  .command('deploy')
  .description('Deploy to an environment')
  .option('env', { type: ['dev', 'staging', 'prod'], default: 'staging' })
  .option('dry-run', { type: 'boolean' })
  .action(({ options }) => {
    // options: { verbose?: boolean; env: …; dryRun?: boolean }
  });

program.start();
```

### 3. Positional arguments + rest passthrough
```ts
program
  .argument('script', { required: true })
  .action(({ args, rest }) => {
    // my-cli build.ts -- --flag-for-the-script x
    // args.script === 'build.ts'; rest === ['--flag-for-the-script', 'x']
    run(args.script, rest);
  });

program.start();
```

### 4. Hook + async action
```ts
program
  .hook(async (options) => { await ensureAuth(options); })
  .option('token', { required: true })
  .action(async ({ options }) => { await deploy(options.token); });

await program.startAsync(); // NOT start() — action/hook are async
```

### 5. Custom parser, injected clock, date option, custom error handler
```ts
program
  .config({
    dateFormat: 'DD/MM/YYYY',
    errorHandler: (errors) => { for (const e of errors) log(e); process.exit(2); },
  })
  .inject('now', () => new Date())
  .option('since', { type: 'date' })                       // → Date
  .option('level', { type: (v) => { if (v === 'x') throw new Error('bad'); return v; } })
  .option('tag', { array: true })                          // → string[]
  .action(({ options }) => { /* options.now, options.since, options.tag */ });

program.start();
```

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Calling `start()` when the action or a hook is async → throws. Use
  `startAsync()`.
- Reading `options['dry-run']` — it is `options.dryRun` (camelCase).
- Annotating the `action` parameter or a function return type — let TS infer.
- Importing internals (`kapitan/src/parser` etc.) — only `program` and the
  exported types are public.
- Expecting comma-split arrays — use repeated flags (`--tag a --tag b`) with
  `array: true`.
- Putting an `.action()` on a `.sub()` group — groups have no action; use
  `.command()` for leaves.
